blind_motion_read: Round 2 rereview: the Wish was already known. Before reading current state descriptions I inspected all 45 decoded display frames in six ordered sheets, plus full-size frames 0,1,2,23,39. The first segment clearly shows the two gear chains orbiting while individual spokes turn, with the central sun, orange rear disc, post and base fixed. Bezel cap positions accompany the carrier. Fine steps resolve the earlier aliasing. Later segments reset the carrier and move small axial hardware, then withdraw a base plate; these are service demonstrations, not stationary-center gear spins. After this fresh read, official state descriptions identify 24 operating samples 0-23 spanning 0 to 64.6875 degrees, then small-cap unscrewing, main-cap unscrewing and lid withdrawal. My initial visual estimate of roughly a quarter turn was approximate; the exact presented segment is 64.6875 degrees, not a full revolution. Forty-eight declared states yield 45 display frames through GIF deduplication. No gross collision appears in observed samples, but this does not prove continuous clearance, drive contact or physical operation. Formal round 4 returned UNVERIFIED (exit 3) with no condition results; precise failure cause is not inferred. Separately, 238 fixed-center BRep contact samples passed, and pedestal/stem full-turn clearance bounds have measured/derived PASS evidence. Continuous/full-coupled drive contact, complete coupled collision clearance and physical transmission remain unverified; this visual pass does not alter those statuses.
